land.text: the county palatine of the Rhine, which the page dates 'From about 1085/86, after the death of the last Ezzonian count palatine'

predecessors.note: The page gives no boundary for the early county palatine; the Rhineland-Palatinate region is a stand-in. Cliopatria draws these lands inside the Holy Roman Empire shape (962..1259), then inside 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' (1260..1806).

successors.note: The Electoral Palatinate stayed a separate member of the Empire in personal union with Bavaria until 1803: France annexed the left bank in 1795 (confirmed at Lunéville, 9 February 1801) and the right bank went to Baden in 1803 (infobox 'Annexed by Baden: 27 April 1803'). Those later steps are Bavaria's events, not recorded here.

capitals.name: Düsseldorf
capitals.note: 'Johann Wilhelm succeeded as elector in 1690, changing his residence first to Düsseldorf'; infobox 1690-1720. Düsseldorf was the capital of Jülich-Berg, which the Neuburg line held in personal union.

correction.text: the Rhenish (Lower) Palatinate: the county palatine of the Rhine around Heidelberg and Mannheim, on both banks of the Rhine

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row. The page dates the county palatine 'From about 1085/86', gives Heidelberg as capital and Alzey as the southernmost point of Ezzonid rule, but no boundary or area; the shape is a radius reading, soft. In 1214 the Wittelsbach duke Louis I of Bavaria was enfeoffed with it (rename event). Revised after review: the Heidelberg 35 km circle also covers the Bergstrasse (Heppenheim is about 26 km away), which was Mainz's until the 1461/1463 pledge, so a 12 km Bergstrasse circle is subtracted here.

correction.text: the Electorate of the Palatinate 'including the Bavarian Upper Palatinate' (Treaty of Pavia 1329): the Lower Palatinate on the Rhine and the Upper Palatinate around Amberg

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Treaty of Pavia (1329) gave the Palatine line the Palatinate with the Upper Palatinate; the Upper Palatinate page says 'the western territory became the Rhenish Palatinate' and the eastern one, 'centred on Amberg', the Upper Palatinate. No area figure on either page. The 1294 division sentence (elder branch gained the Rhenish Palatinate and the Bavarian Nordgau) is not drawn before 1329 because the treaty is the first page to place the Upper Palatinate with the Palatine line in a dated grant. Revised after review: the Upper Palatinate circle was cut from 70 km (about 15,400 km2, 1.6 times the region) to 55 km (about 9,500 km2); the Bergstrasse (Mainz's until 1461/1463) is subtracted from the Heidelberg circle.

correction.text: the Palatinate with the Bergstrasse towns (Lorsch, Heppenheim, Bensheim) received in the Treaty of Zeilsheim, October 1463

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the Mainz Diocesan Feud 'Frederick I received Lorsch, Heppenheim, and Bensheim for his assistance'; a 20 km circle at 8.62E 49.66N stands for the three towns. The pages opened do not say when Mainz recovered them (the Mainz dossier does not draw them after 1463), so they stay here. Revised after review: Upper Palatinate circle 55 km (was 70); the 12 km Bergstrasse circle (was 20, which reached Worms) is already inside the Heidelberg circle and is kept so the gain event has its own region; the shape ends 1622 because K3 starts in 1623.

correction.text: the Lower Palatinate alone, under Spanish and Bavarian occupation, after the Upper Palatinate and the electoral vote passed to Maximilian of Bavaria; the Bergstrasse (Lorsch, Heppenheim, Bensheim) is back with Mainz from 1623 and is taken out of the circle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in February 1623 Frederick V lost the electoral vote and the Upper Palatinate was Bavarian ('Over the period 1621-1622, the Palatinate was occupied by Spanish and Bavarian troops'). The land is still the state's by right, hatched as occupied (occupation events 1621-1648/1652) rather than redrawn. Revised after review: the Bergstrasse is no longer drawn Palatine from 1623, when the pledge ended (Heppenheim page: 'an interruption from 1461 to 1623').

correction.text: the Lower Palatinate restored by the Peace of Westphalia: 'he regained the Lower Palatinate and the title Elector Palatine'; the Upper Palatinate stays Bavarian; the Bergstrasse stays Mainz's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 24 October 1648 restores the Lower Palatinate to Charles I Louis; Spanish troops stay at Frankenthal-area garrisons until 1652 (Palatinate campaign page). France contests the Rhenish lands from September 1688 (contest events), so the shape is the de jure state.

correction.text: the Lower Palatinate with the duchy of Palatinate-Neuburg on the Danube, merged in 1685 when Philip William of Neuburg became Elector Palatine; the Bergstrasse stays Mainz's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Neuburg infobox says 'Merged with the Electorate of the Palatinate: 1685'. Jülich and Berg (held by the Neuburg line since 1653) and the Sulzbach lands (which came to Bavaria in 1777) are in personal union and are not drawn here; a gap-filler should give Jülich-Berg its own dossier.

ledger.note: 1085: the county palatine of the Rhine begins. The page dates the Palatinate 'From about 1085/86, after the death of the last Ezzonian count palatine'; Heidelberg is the infobox capital, the southernmost point of Ezzonid rule near Alzey.

region.text: the Rhenish Palatinate on the Rhine (Heidelberg, Alzey), no boundary on the page

ledger.note: About 1182: Conrad moves the residence from Stahleck Castle near Bacharach to Heidelberg.

1214: the Palatinate passes to the Wittelsbachs. 'When Henry's son Henry the Younger died without heirs in 1214' the Hohenstaufen king Frederick II enfeoffed Duke Louis I of Bavaria with it (the enfeoffment year is the page's context, not a stated date); Otto II of Bavaria married Agnes of the Palatinate in 1222. Same state, new dynasty.

1329: the Treaty of Pavia gives the Palatine line the Upper Palatinate. 'Louis IV granted the Electorate of the Palatinate (including the Bavarian Upper Palatinate) to Rudolph's descendants'; the Upper Palatinate page: 'By the 1329 Treaty of Pavia, the Wittelsbach territories were divided between two branches', the eastern territory centred on Amberg. The 1294 division among the heirs of Louis II (elder branch: Rhenish Palatinate and the Nordgau) is on the Electoral Palatinate page.

region.text: the Bavarian Upper Palatinate (Nordgau) around Amberg

ledger.note: 10 January 1356: the Golden Bull makes the Palatinate an electorate. 'In the Golden Bull of 1356, the Palatinate was recognized as one of the secular electorates' with the offices of archsteward and imperial vicar; infobox 'Confirmed as Electorate: 10 January 1356'; the Pavia page adds that only the Palatine line was invested with the electoral dignity.

October 1463: the Palatinate takes the Bergstrasse. In the Treaty of Zeilsheim ending the Mainz Diocesan Feud 'A number of castles and towns were transferred to the Palatinate, Hesse and, briefly, even Saxony'; Frederick I 'received Lorsch, Heppenheim, and Bensheim' for his assistance to Adolf of Nassau. The Mainz Diocesan Feud page gives no date for the transfer itself. The Heppenheim page dates the pledge: 'an interruption from 1461 to 1623 when the fief was pledged to the Electorate of the Palatinate' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heppenheim), so the pledge is 1461 and the Zeilsheim settlement 1463; 1463 is kept as the year of the treaty and the confidence is 2.

region.text: Lorsch, Heppenheim and Bensheim on the Bergstrasse

ledger.note: 1559: the electorate passes to Frederick III of Simmern. 'When the senior branch of the family died out in 1559, the electorate passed to Frederick III'; same state, cadet line (the page also lists the early-16th-century cadet lines at Simmern, Kaiserslautern and Zweibrucken in the Lower Palatinate and Neuburg and Sulzbach in the Upper).

1621: Spanish troops hold the west of the Palatinate. 'Over the period 1621-1622, the Palatinate was occupied by Spanish and Bavarian troops' after Frederick V's Bohemian defeat in 1620; the Palatinate campaign page dates the campaign from 30 August 1620 and says the Spanish took the west.

region.text: the Lower Palatinate west of the Rhine, taken by the Spanish army from the Spanish Netherlands

ledger.note: 19 September 1622: Heidelberg falls to the Catholic army. 'Heidelberg fell on 19 September 1622' after 11 weeks of resistance; the Electoral Palatinate page names the occupiers as Spanish and Bavarian troops.

region.text: Heidelberg and the Lower Palatinate east of the Rhine

ledger.note: 1623: the Bergstrasse pledge ends and Heppenheim is Mainz's again. 'But for an interruption from 1461 to 1623 when the fief was pledged to the Electorate of the Palatinate, Heppenheim remained an Electoral Mainz holding' until 1803. The page names only Heppenheim; Lorsch and Bensheim, pledged with it in 1463, are the author's reading.

region.text: Lorsch, Heppenheim and Bensheim on the Bergstrasse, the 1463 gain pledged back to Mainz

ledger.note: February 1623: Maximilian of Bavaria takes the Upper Palatinate and the electoral vote. 'In February 1623, Ferdinand removed Frederick as one of the seven Imperial Prince-electors, his vote going to Maximilian of Bavaria' (Palatinate campaign page); the Upper Palatinate page: forfeited in 1619-1620 and given to the Duke of Bavaria, and 'the Upper Palatinate remained under the Elector of Bavaria' in 1648 and since.

region.text: the Upper Palatinate around Amberg, forfeit to the Emperor and given to the Duke of Bavaria

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: the Lower Palatinate returns to the Elector Palatine. 'When the Peace of Westphalia ended the war in 1648, he regained the Lower Palatinate and the title Elector Palatine' (Westphalia infobox: 15 May-24 October 1648); the Bavarian garrisons leave, the Upper Palatinate stays with Bavaria.

region.text: the Lower Palatinate along the Rhine, regained by Charles I Louis

ledger.note: 1652: the last Spanish troops leave. 'Spanish occupation of Palatinate wouldn't end until 1652 (after Peace of Westphalia).'

region.text: the western Lower Palatinate held by Spain since 1621

ledger.note: 1685: Palatinate-Neuburg merges with the electorate. Infobox 'Merged with the Electorate of the Palatinate: 1685'; the ruler list reads 'Philip William, 1653-90 (also Duke of Jülich and Berg from 1653 and Elector Palatine from 1685)' after the Simmern line died out. The Neuburg lands are a radius reading around Neuburg an der Donau.

region.text: the duchy of Palatinate-Neuburg on the Danube, created in 1505 after the Landshut War of Succession

ledger.note: September 1688: Louis XIV invades the Palatinate. 'In September 1688 Louis led an army across the Rhine'; Philippsburg was besieged on 27 September and Mannheim 'capitulated on 11 November, shortly followed by Frankenthal'; Louis claimed the Palatinate for his sister-in-law Elizabeth Charlotte.

region.text: the Rhenish Palatinate: Philippsburg, Mannheim, Frankenthal, Heidelberg

ledger.note: 1690: Johann Wilhelm moves the residence from Heidelberg to Düsseldorf (infobox 'Düsseldorf; (1690-1720)').

1697: the Peace of Ryswick ends the fighting. French troops destroyed Heidelberg on 2 March 1689 and Mannheim on 8 March, raided the Palatinate again in 1693 (Heidelberg fell 22 May 1693) and 'France later renounced its claim to the region in the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick' (Electoral Palatinate page).

30 December 1777: the Palatinate passes to Bavaria. Infobox 'Subsumed by Bavaria: 30 December 1777'; Charles Theodore, Duke of Sulzbach and Elector Palatine since 1742, 'inherited the Electorate of Bavaria in 1777'. The Upper Palatinate page: Neuburg and Sulzbach 'came to Bavaria in 1777'.

region.text: the Lower Palatinate and the Neuburg and Sulzbach lands, now joined to the Bavarian Electorate in personal union

wars.name: Palatinate campaign

zones.text: the Lower Palatinate: Wimpfen 8 May and Hochst in June 1622, Heidelberg 19 September 1622, Mannheim; Stadtlohn 6 August 1623

wars.outcome: Catholic victory: the Palatinate is occupied, Frederick V is removed as elector in February 1623 and the Upper Palatinate goes to Bavaria; the Spanish stay in the west until 1652.
wars.note: The campaign runs '30 August 1620 - 27 August 1623' on the page; the Upper Palatinate and Bohemian fighting are not described there.

wars.name: Nine Years' War

zones.text: the Rhenish Palatinate: Philippsburg, Mannheim, Frankenthal, Heidelberg

wars.outcome: France invades in September 1688, burns Heidelberg and Mannheim in March 1689 and raids again in 1693; by the 1697 Peace of Ryswick France gives up 'gains on the right bank of the Rhine' and its Palatinate claim.
wars.note: The page gives no Palatinate-specific clause of the treaty; the claim renunciation is on the Electoral Palatinate page.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and lines of succession, no boundaries; the Palatinate is a patchwork of scattered lands. The 1329 split between the Rhenish and Upper Palatinate is the one dated frontier.
The Peace of Westphalia (1648) fixed the Lower Palatinate and left the Upper Palatinate with Bavaria; enclave and cadet-line frontiers inside the state remain approximate.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (7 pages opened). New state: Cliopatria has no Palatinate row; its lands sit inside 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' (1260..1806) and, from 1777, Bavaria.

SCOPE CHOICE. The dossier starts at 1085 (the page's 'From about 1085/86') and ends 30 December 1777, the infobox 'Subsumed by Bavaria'. The electorate lived on as a separate member of the Empire in personal union with Bavaria until 1803 (left bank annexed by France 1795, Lunéville 9 February 1801, right bank to Baden 27 April 1803); those steps are left to the Bavarian dossier because Cliopatria and the sibling HRE-minor-states ledger already give the Palatinate to Bavaria from 1777.

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS. The gazetteer has no 'Upper Palatinate' or 'Amberg'; the Bergstrasse is a 20 km circle at 8.62E 49.66N, the Upper Palatinate is a 70 km circle at 11.86E 49.44N and the Neuburg lands a 35 km circle at 11.18E 48.73N. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Upper Palatinate' (region, Oberpfalz, centred on Amberg), 'Lower Palatinate' (region), 'Neuburg an der Donau' (place), 'Amberg' (place). The Lower Palatinate is the Rhineland-Palatinate region within 75 km of Mannheim plus a 35 km circle at Heidelberg (about 11,000 km2), a stand-in: the real electorate was scattered and the left bank included Kaiserslautern, Alzey and Neustadt (the page names only Alzey).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The early-16th-century cadet principalities Simmern, Kaiserslautern, Zweibrucken (Lower Palatinate) and Neuburg, Sulzbach (Upper Palatinate) are named on the page; Palatinate-Zweibrucken and Palatinate-Simmern are separate states that need dossiers (they held land for centuries) and are not subtracted from the keyframes. (2) Jülich-Berg, held by the Neuburg line from 1653, is a personal union drawn nowhere here; it needs its own dossier. (3) The Landshut War of 1503-1505 (Palatine losses and the creation of Neuburg) and the Palatine Neumarkt line were not on the pages opened. (4) The 1329 Pavia sentence says 'returned the Palatinate to his nephews': the pages do not say when Louis IV had taken it, so the 1294 Nordgau acquisition is recorded in a note only. (5) Heidelberg is the infobox capital 1085-1690, but the text dates the move from Stahleck to about 1182, hence the Stahleck span at confidence 1. (6) Rulers: the page lists only the first (Henry of Laach, 1085-1095) and the last elector (Maximilian Joseph, 1799-1803); a ruler list was not opened, so none is given.

COUNTERPARTS FOR OTHER GROUPS: palatinate-neuburg, duchy-of-palatinate-zweibrucken, julich-berg (the 1777 hand-over of Jülich and Berg to Bavaria is in the eu-09-c ledger), kingdom-of-spain (the Spanish Netherlands army that occupied the west 1621-1652).

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). (1) Upper Palatinate circle cut from 70 to 55 km (the 70 km circle was 1.6 times the region). (2) The Bergstrasse pledge ended in 1623 (Heppenheim page: 'an interruption from 1461 to 1623'); a 1623 loss to electorate-of-mainz is entered and the Bergstrasse (12 km circle at 8.62E 49.66N, cut from 20 km because that reached Worms) is subtracted from the Lower Palatinate before 1461/63 and after 1623, since the 35 km Heidelberg circle covers it. The 1463 gain is confidence 2: the Mainz Diocesan Feud page gives no date for the transfer, the Heppenheim page dates the pledge 1461. (3) K2 'to' is 1622 (applied by the reviewer's fix). DISAGREEMENT: none.
